text: A. Request approval for out-of-state travel for one (1) Utilities Division Analyst to attend the 2026 World of Coal Ash conference in Lexington, KY, May 4 – May 7, 2026. The World of Coal Ash is the premier international conference on the science, application, and sustainability of coal combustion products. The total estimated cost of $2,896 will be paid pursuant to the July 29, 2019, MOU in Docket No. 42310, therefore leaving no direct cost to the state. Dates of travel: May 3 - May 7, 2026. (page 1)

B. Request approval for out-of-state travel for six (6) Electric Unit Staff members to attend the SEARUC 2026 Annual Education Conference in Biloxi, MS, May 17 – May 20, 2026. The forum will focus on topics relevant to Staff's work and continuing educational needs. The total estimated cost of $15,400 will be paid pursuant to the June 28, 2023, MOU in Docket No. 44280, therefore leaving no direct cost to the state. Dates of travel: May 16 – May 20, 2026. (page 2)
C. Request approval for out-of-state travel for two (2) Electric Unit Staff
members to attend the 2026 NARUC Staff Subcommittee on
Accounting and Finance in Charlotte, NC, April 19 – April 23, 2026.
The purpose of the conference is to provide accounting, finance,
and utility regulatory information to personnel with all levels of
experience who work in the utility regulatory environment. The total
estimated cost of $4,438 will be paid pursuant to the June 28, 2023,
MOU in Docket No. 44280, therefore leaving no direct cost to the
state. Dates of travel: April 19 – April 23, 2026. (page 3)
D. Request approval for out-of-state travel for one (1) EERE Unit Staff
member to attend the NARUC 2026 Spring Rate School in
Coronado, CA, May 10 – May 15, 2026. Staff member is a part of
the Rate School Faculty and will present on Rate Design and be a
Coach during the school. The total estimated cost is $2,909. Of that
cost, $2,500 will be covered by NARUC. The remaining balance of
$409 will be paid pursuant to the June 28, 2023, MOU in Docket Nos.
44160 and 44161, therefore leaving no direct cost to the state. Dates
E. Request approval for out-of-state travel for one (1) Electric Unit Staff
member to attend the 2026 IEEE T&D PES (Power & Energy Society)
Conference in Chicago, IL, May 3 - May 7, 2026. This technical
conference will cover topics such as Grid Infrastructure and
Maintenance, Cyber and Physical Security, DER Integration, Energy
Storage Systems, T&D Planning and Reliable System Design. The
total estimated cost of $2,935 will be paid pursuant to the June 28,
2023, MOU in Docket No. 44280, therefore leaving no direct cost to
the state. Dates of travel: May 2 - May 7, 2026. (page 5)

F. Request to purchase the Proofpoint Core Email Protection subscription. This purchase supports our ongoing cybersecurity posture, provides critical email security capabilities including threat protection, URL and attachment defense, automated threat response, and aligns with the State of Georgia’s approved software contracts. The product also includes InfoSec implementation services and Log API forwarding at no additional cost, as was recently required by Georgia Technology Authority. The vendor is an approved provider of this product within the State of Georgia procurement system. The total cost of the product is $17,591.

text: A. Request approval to purchase five (5) 2026 Chevrolet Tahoes for approximately $55,837 each for a total of $279,185. Necessary options and required aftermarket safety and emergency equipment will be approximately $8,500 per vehicle for a total of $42,500 for a Grand Total of $321,685. Pursuant to the approval of the Department of Administrative Services, certain vehicles are identified for replacement based on age, high mileage or excessive repair costs. We currently have seven (7) vehicles within our fleet that have been identified as eligible for replacement. Two (2) of these vehicles have recently received transmission replacements so we are seeking approval to replace only five (5) of the eligible vehicles. The vehicles will be used to inspect natural gas operators for compliance with the minimum federal safety standards, state laws and Commission rules. Funds from the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) will fund this purchase. (pages 1 – 16)

The total estimated cost of $1,004 will be paid pursuant to the June 28, 2023, MOU in Docket Nos. 44160 and 44161, therefore leaving no direct cost to the state. Dates of travel: September 9 – September 11, 2026. (page 5)

members to attend the 2026 NARUC Annual Meeting and Education Conference in San Juan, Puerto Rico, November 8 – November 11, 2026. One staff member serves as the Vice Chair of NARUC’s Natural Gas Subcommittee and will support the Subcommittee Chair. This conference is designed to equip staff with the latest insights into national developments, emerging trends, and regulatory best practices. The total estimated cost of $5,568 will be paid pursuant to the January 28, 2021, Stipulation in Docket No. 42315, therefore leaving no direct cost to the state. Dates of travel: November 7 – November 11, 2026. (page 6)

Staff are also members of NARUC Staff Subcommittees that will meet at the summit. The total estimated cost of $17,430 will be paid pursuant to the June 28, 2023, MOU in Docket No. 44280, therefore leaving no direct cost to the state. Dates of travel: November 7 – November 11, 2026. the Pipeline Safety reimbursement (to be charged to Unit 6). Dates

B. Request approval to purchase three (3) 2025 Chevrolet Tahoes for approximately $55,837 each for a total of $167,511. Necessary options and required aftermarket safety and emergency equipment will be approximately $16,515 per vehicle for a total of $49,545 for the Grand Total of $217,056. One of the vehicles is being provided for the new inspector position that was approved in the FY 2026 budget. Another vehicle is replacing a vehicle that was involved in an accident and the insurance adjuster has totaled the vehicle. The other vehicle will be replacing a vehicle that is being surplussed due to high mileage and maintenance costs pursuant to DOAS guidelines. The vehicles will be used to inspect natural gas operators for compliance with the minimum federal safety standards, state laws and Commission rules. Funds from the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) will fund most of this purchase along with approximately $39,742 of state funding included in the FY 2026 budget for the new inspector position and approximately $14,825 for the insurance claim on the totaled vehicle. text: A. Request approval to purchase five (5) 2026 Chevrolet Tahoes for approximately $55,837 each for a total of $279,185. Necessary options and required aftermarket safety and emergency equipment will be approximately $8,500 per vehicle for a total of $42,500 for a Grand Total of $321,685. Pursuant to the approval of the Department of Administrative Services, certain vehicles are identified for replacement based on age, high mileage or excessive repair costs. We currently have seven (7) vehicles within our fleet that have been identified as eligible for replacement. Two (2) of these vehicles have recently received transmission replacements so we are seeking approval to replace only five (5) of the eligible vehicles. The vehicles will be used to inspect natural gas operators for compliance with the minimum federal safety standards, state laws and Commission rules. Funds from the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) will fund this purchase. (pages 1 – 16)

A. Request approval to initiate a consulting contract to provide professional consulting assistance to Commission Staff. This assistance includes issues relating to cost of service, the addition of Large Load customers, and other issues that may arise prior to the 2028 Integrated Resource Plan and Rate Case. The contract is not to exceed the amount of $100,000, which will be paid pursuant to the June 28, 2023, MOU in Docket No. 44280, therefore leaving no direct cost to the state. (page 17 -24)
A. Request approval of the minutes from February 3, 2026, and February 18, 2026, Administrative Sessions.

text: A. Request approval for out-of-state travel for one (1) Utilities Division Analyst to attend the 2026 World of Coal Ash conference in Lexington, KY, May 4 – May 7, 2026. The World of Coal Ash is the premier international conference on the science, application, and sustainability of coal combustion products. The total estimated cost of $2,896 will be paid pursuant to the July 29, 2019, MOU in Docket No. 42310, therefore leaving no direct cost to the state. Dates of travel: May 3 - May 7, 2026. (page 1)

B. Request approval for out-of-state travel for six (6) Electric Unit Staff members to attend the SEARUC 2026 Annual Education Conference in Biloxi, MS, May 17 – May 20, 2026. The forum will focus on topics relevant to Staff's work and continuing educational needs. The total estimated cost of $15,400 will be paid pursuant to the June 28, 2023, MOU in Docket No. 44280, therefore leaving no direct cost to the state. Dates of travel: May 16 – May 20, 2026. (page 2)
C. Request approval for out-of-state travel for two (2) Electric Unit Staff
members to attend the 2026 NARUC Staff Subcommittee on
Accounting and Finance in Charlotte, NC, April 19 – April 23, 2026.
The purpose of the conference is to provide accounting, finance,
and utility regulatory information to personnel with all levels of
experience who work in the utility regulatory environment. The total
estimated cost of $4,438 will be paid pursuant to the June 28, 2023,
MOU in Docket No. 44280, therefore leaving no direct cost to the
state. Dates of travel: April 19 – April 23, 2026. (page 3)
D. Request approval for out-of-state travel for one (1) EERE Unit Staff
member to attend the NARUC 2026 Spring Rate School in
Coronado, CA, May 10 – May 15, 2026. Staff member is a part of
the Rate School Faculty and will present on Rate Design and be a
Coach during the school. The total estimated cost is $2,909. Of that
cost, $2,500 will be covered by NARUC. The remaining balance of
$409 will be paid pursuant to the June 28, 2023, MOU in Docket Nos.
44160 and 44161, therefore leaving no direct cost to the state. Dates
E. Request approval for out-of-state travel for one (1) Electric Unit Staff
member to attend the 2026 IEEE T&D PES (Power & Energy Society)
Conference in Chicago, IL, May 3 - May 7, 2026. This technical
conference will cover topics such as Grid Infrastructure and
Maintenance, Cyber and Physical Security, DER Integration, Energy
Storage Systems, T&D Planning and Reliable System Design. The
total estimated cost of $2,935 will be paid pursuant to the June 28,
2023, MOU in Docket No. 44280, therefore leaving no direct cost to
the state. Dates of travel: May 2 - May 7, 2026. (page 5)

F. Request to purchase the Proofpoint Core Email Protection subscription. This purchase supports our ongoing cybersecurity posture, provides critical email security capabilities including threat protection, URL and attachment defense, automated threat response, and aligns with the State of Georgia’s approved software contracts. The product also includes InfoSec implementation services and Log API forwarding at no additional cost, as was recently required by Georgia Technology Authority. The vendor is an approved provider of this product within the State of Georgia procurement system. The total cost of the product is $17,591.

text: A. Request approval for out-of-state travel for one (1) EERE Unit Staff member to attend the 2026 National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners (“NARUC”) Summer Policy Summit in Minneapolis, MN, July 19 – July 22, 2026. This conference will provide training on topics including renewable energy and storage, affordability, and other pertinent regulatory topics. The total estimated cost of $2,364 will be paid pursuant to the June 28, 2023, MOU in Docket Nos. 44160 and 44161, therefore leaving no direct cost to the state. Dates of travel: July 18 – July 22, 2026. (page 1)
B. Request approval for out-of-state travel for five (5) Electric Unit Staff

members to attend the 2026 National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners (“NARUC”) Summer Policy Summit in Minneapolis, MN, July 19 – July 22, 2026. Topics at conference include large load policy issues, transmission planning and interconnection, and prospects for future development of renewable and nuclear energy. Staff are also members of NARUC Staff Subcommittees. The total estimated cost of $15,003 will be paid pursuant to the June 28, 2023, MOU in Docket No. 44280, therefore leaving no direct cost to the state. Dates of travel: July 18 – July 22, 2026. (page 2)
C. Request approval for out-of-state travel for one (1) Natural Gas Unit
Staff member to attend the 2026 National Association of Regulatory

Utility Commissioners (“NARUC”) Summer Policy Summit in Minneapolis, MN, July 19 – July 22, 2026. Staff member is the Vice Chair of the NARUC Natural Gas Subcommittee. Expected topics include empowering state public service commissions in navigating resiliency, affordability, reliability, permitting, siting, and cybersecurity. The total estimated cost of $3,003 will be paid pursuant to the January 28, 2021, Stipulation in

E. Request approval for out-of-state travel for one (1) Utilities Division Staff member to attend the 2026 National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners (“NARUC”) Summer Policy Summit on July 19 – July 22, 2026, in Minneapolis, MN. The staff member is a member of the NARUC Critical Infrastructure Staff Subcommittee which will hold their quarterly meeting to discuss keeping systems in place that are vital for a country to function when there may be a devastating failure. In addition, the remaining days of the conference will be attendance at various educational/training opportunities. The total estimated cost to attend is $3,200. Dates of travel: July 18 – July 22, 2026. (page 5)

F. Request approval for out-of-state travel for one (1) Utilities Division Staff member to attend the 2026 National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners (“NARUC”) Summer Policy Summit on July 19 – July 22, 2026, in Minneapolis, MN. The staff member is a member of the NARUC Subcommittee on Pipeline Safety and the Subcommittee on Energy Resources & the Environment, which will hold their quarterly meetings and will be conducting educational sessions and panel discussions to enhance staff expertise on regulatory topics. The total estimated cost to attend is $3,264. Dates of travel: July 18 – July 22, 2026. (page 6)

Request approval for out-of-state travel for one (1) Administrative Unit Staff member to attend the 2026 National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners (“NARUC”) Summer Policy Meeting on July 19 – July 22, 2026, in Minneapolis, MN. The staff member serves as the Co-Chair of the NARUC Education and Research Subcommittee which will hold their quarterly meeting to discuss educational opportunities, and grant scholarships. In addition, the remaining days of the conference will be attendance at various educational/training opportunities. The total estimated cost to attend is $3,264 which will be paid pursuant to the June 28, 2023, MOU in Docket No. 44280 therefore leaving no direct cost to the state. Dates of travel: July 18 – July 22, 2026. (page 7)

In addition, the remaining days of the conference will be attendance at various educational/training opportunities. text: A. Request approval for out-of-state travel for one (1) Pipeline Safety Unit Staff member to attend the 2026 NAPSR National Regional Meeting in Madison, WI, September 21 - September 25, 2026. The total estimated cost of $3,024 will be principally federally funded through the Pipeline Safety reimbursement (to be charged to Unit 6). Dates of travel: September 20 - September 25, 2026. (page 1)

professional construction monitoring and projects controls consulting
assistance to the Commission Staff in Docket No. 56818: Georgia
Power Company's Plant Wansley Units 10 and 11. In accordance
with O.C.G.A. § 46-2-33(0), the per case per year maximum for

contract authorizes a Work Plan of approximately $363,000 per year,

B. Request approval for out-of-state travel for two (2) EERE Staff

members to attend the 2026 NARUC Annual Meeting and Education Conference in San Juan, Puerto Rico, November 8 – November 11, 2026. This policy summit will provide Staff with the opportunity to learn the most up-to-date information on relevant topics in the renewable energy and energy storage industries as well as data center and rate related items. The total estimated cost of $5,477 will be paid pursuant to the June 28, 2023, MOU in Docket Nos. 44160 and 44161, therefore leaving no direct cost to the state.

This conference will have a focus on load growth from large load customers. The staff member will be giving a presentation on the decision-making frameworks behind grid investment and procurement. The total estimated cost of $1,004 will be paid pursuant to the June 28, 2023, MOU in Docket Nos. 44160 and 44161, therefore leaving no direct cost to the state. Dates of travel: September 9 – September 11, 2026. (page 5)

members to attend the 2026 NARUC Annual Meeting and Education Conference in San Juan, Puerto Rico, November 8 – November 11, 2026. One staff member serves as the Vice Chair of NARUC’s Natural Gas Subcommittee and will support the Subcommittee Chair. This conference is designed to equip staff with the latest insights into national developments, emerging trends, and regulatory best practices. The total estimated cost of $5,568 will be paid pursuant to the January 28, 2021, Stipulation in Docket No. 42315, therefore leaving no direct cost to the state. Dates of travel: November 7 – November 11, 2026. (page 6)

Request approval for out-of-state travel for six (6) Electric Unit Staff members to attend the 2026 NARUC Annual Meeting and Education Conference in San Juan, Puerto Rico, November 8 – November 11, 2026. Staff are also members of NARUC Staff Subcommittees that will meet at the summit. The total estimated cost of $17,430 will be paid pursuant to the June 28, 2023, MOU in Docket No. 44280, therefore leaving no direct cost to the state. Dates of travel: November 7 – November 11, 2026. (page 7)

text: |Contact: Tom Krause |Georgia Public Service Commission |244 Washington St S.W. |
PSC to Hold Sept. 15 Meeting/Public Forum in Savannah
August 25, 2026 – (ATLANTA) The Georgia Public Service Commission will hold its Administrative Session as well as a special public forum in Savannah on Tuesday, Sept. 15.

At the public forum, Georgians will have the opportunity to address the Commission with any comments or concerns. Each participant will be limited to three minutes so everyone who wants to speak will have the chance.

The Administrative Session and forum will be simulcast in the Atlanta hearing room for anyone who would like to watch in the Commission’s usual venue. Those viewing from Atlanta will not be able to participate in the forum. Like all meetings of the PSC, the session and forum will be live streamed on the Commission’s YouTube page.
The suggestion to hold a session in the southern part of the state was proposed by Commissioner Alicia Johnson, who lives in Savannah. Chairman Jason Shaw, who lives in Lakeland, embraced the idea.

“During the public comments portion of our meetings, I’m always impressed by the number of people who drive from the four corners of our state, just to offer their opinion,” Chairman Shaw said. “As someone who drives to Atlanta weekly from South Georgia, I know the effort it takes. I’m glad the PSC will be driving to the people for a change.”
Commissioner Johnson likewise stressed the importance of bringing government to the people – specifically to her hometown.

“Coastal Georgia is experiencing tremendous growth,” Commissioner Johnson said. “It’s facing consequential decisions about energy, infrastructure, affordability, resilience, and our economic future. The people who live, work, raise families, and build businesses here deserve a meaningful opportunity to engage directly with the Commission making decisions that affect their monthly bills and their communities. This meeting represents an important step toward a PSC that is present, accessible, and accountable to people in every region of our state. Public service should meet people where they are, and on September 15, we are bringing the people’s Commission to Coastal Georgia.”
Date and Time: 9:30 a.m. - noon, Tuesday, Sept. 15
Location: Chatham County Administrative Building, 124 Bull St., Savannah, GA, 31401
